nodes.title: Magnetic Flux & Faraday's Laws
points: Magnetic flux Φ through an area A: Φ = B · A = BA cosθ, where θ is angle between magnetic field B and area normal. SI unit: Weber (Wb = T·m² = V·s). Dimensions: [M¹L²T⁻²I⁻¹].
Faraday's First Law: Whenever magnetic flux linked with a closed circuit changes, an induced EMF is produced in the circuit.
Faraday's Second Law: The magnitude of induced EMF is directly proportional to the time rate of change of magnetic flux linked with the circuit: e ∝ dΦ/dt.
For a coil of N turns: e = −N (dΦ/dt). The negative sign is given by Lenz's law.

nodes.title: Lenz's Law & Energy Conservation
points: Lenz's Law: The direction of induced current is always such that it OPPOSES the change in magnetic flux that produces it.
Lenz's law is a consequence of the Law of Conservation of Energy: Mechanical work done against the opposing magnetic force is converted into electrical energy.
When North pole of magnet approaches a coil: Near face develops NORTH polarity (repels magnet, work done against repulsion).
When North pole of magnet recedes from a coil: Near face develops SOUTH polarity (attracts magnet, work done against attraction).
Fleming's Right-Hand Rule (Generator Rule): Thumb = Motion, Forefinger = Magnetic Field, Central Finger = Induced Current.

nodes.title: Motional EMF in Straight Conductors
points: Motional EMF: EMF induced across ends of a conductor of length L moving with velocity v perpendicular to magnetic field B: e = BLv.
If velocity v makes angle θ with magnetic field B: e = BLv sinθ.
Induced current in closed circuit of resistance R: I = e / R = BLv / R.
Magnetic braking force opposing motion: F = I L B = B² L² v / R.
Mechanical power required to pull conductor: P_mech = F v = B² L² v² / R.
Joule heat dissipated in circuit: P_elect = I² R = B² L² v² / R = P_mech (demonstrates energy conservation).

nodes.title: Induced EMF in Rotating Conductors
points: A conducting rod of length L rotating with angular speed ω about one end in a perpendicular magnetic field B sweeps area at rate dA/dt = ½ L² ω.
Induced EMF across ends of rotating rod: e = dΦ/dt = B (dA/dt) = ½ B ω L² = B π L² n (where n is frequency of rotation).
A conducting disc of radius R rotating in perpendicular magnetic field B: EMF between center and rim: e = ½ B ω R².
Earth's magnetic field component: Vertical component B_v induces EMF across axle of moving train or wingspan of flying airplane: e = B_v L v.

formulas.label: Rotating rod EMF
formulas.expr: e = ½ B ω L² = B π L² n

nodes.title: Eddy Currents (Foucault Currents)
points: Eddy currents are closed circulating currents induced in bulk metallic pieces when subjected to changing magnetic flux.
Discovered by Leon Foucault. Produce significant Joule heating (I²R loss) in cores of transformers and motors.
Minimizing Eddy Currents: Use laminated magnetic cores made of thin insulated sheets (laminations) perpendicular to current paths.

Useful Applications: (1) Electromagnetic damping in dead-beat galvanometers; (2) Induction furnaces for melting metals; (3) Magnetic brakes in high-speed trains; (4) Electric power meters (rotating aluminium disc).

nodes.title: Self-Inductance & Solenoid Inductor
points: Self-induction: Phenomenon in which changing current in a coil induces a back EMF in the SAME coil opposing the change.
Magnetic flux linkage: N Φ = L I ⟹ Back EMF e = −L (dI/dt).
Coefficient of self-inductance L: Ratio of back EMF to rate of change of current: L = |e| / (dI/dt). SI unit: Henry (H = V·s/A = Wb/A). Dimensions: [M¹L²T⁻²I⁻²].
Self-inductance of long solenoid: L = μ₀ n² A l = μ₀ (N² / l) A, where n = N/l is turns per unit length.
Energy stored in an inductor: U = ½ L I² (stored in the form of magnetic field inside core).
Magnetic energy density: u_B = B² / (2μ₀) (energy per unit volume of magnetic field).

formulas.label: Self-inductance of solenoid
formulas.expr: L = μ₀ n² A l = μ₀ (N² A / l)

nodes.title: Mutual Inductance & Coupling Coefficient
points: Mutual induction: Phenomenon in which changing current in primary coil induces an EMF in neighbouring secondary coil.
Flux linkage in secondary: N₂ Φ₂ = M I₁ ⟹ Induced EMF in secondary: e₂ = −M (dI₁/dt).
Coefficient of mutual inductance M: M = |e₂| / (dI₁/dt). SI unit: Henry (H). Reciprocity theorem: M₁₂ = M₂₁ = M.
Mutual inductance of two coaxial solenoids: M = μ₀ n₁ n₂ A l = μ₀ N₁ N₂ A / l.
Coupling Coefficient k: Indicates extent of magnetic flux linkage between coils: k = M / √(L₁ L₂), where 0 ≤ k ≤ 1.
k = 1 for tight coupling (100% flux linkage); k = 0 for perpendicular/distant coils (no coupling).

formulas.label: Mutual inductance solenoids
formulas.expr: M = μ₀ n₁ n₂ A l

nodes.title: AC Generator (Alternator) Working & Principle
points: Principle: Converts mechanical energy into alternating electrical energy based on electromagnetic induction.
A rectangular coil of N turns and area A rotates with constant angular speed ω in uniform magnetic field B.
Magnetic flux at time t: Φ(t) = N B A cos(ωt).
Induced EMF: e = −dΦ/dt = N B A ω sin(ωt) = e₀ sin(ωt), where peak EMF e₀ = N B A ω = 2π n N B A.
Essential Components: (1) Armature coil, (2) Strong field magnet, (3) Slip rings, (4) Carbon brushes.
EMF is zero when coil plane is perpendicular to B (flux is maximum); EMF is maximum when coil plane is parallel to B (flux is zero).

nodes.title: Must-Know Board Derivations & Circuit Diagrams
points: Board Favourite #1: Derive expression for motional EMF induced in a conductor moving perpendicular to uniform magnetic field: e = BLv.
Board Favourite #2: Derive expression for induced EMF in a rotating rod about one end: e = ½ B ω L².
Board Favourite #3: Derive expression for self-inductance of a long solenoid L = μ₀ n² A l and magnetic energy stored U = ½ LI².
Board Favourite #4: Derive expression for mutual inductance between two long coaxial solenoids: M = μ₀ n₁ n₂ A l.
Board Favourite #5: Explain AC Generator principle, construction, working, and derive e = e₀ sin(ωt) with waveform graph.

nodes.title: MHT-CET Shortcuts, Flux-Charge Hacks & Traps
points: Induced Charge Shortcut: Total charge q flowing through a circuit during flux change ΔΦ depends ONLY on net flux change and resistance: q = ΔΦ / R (completely INDEPENDENT of time taken!).
Induced Electric Field: A time-varying magnetic field creates a NON-CONSERVATIVE electric field: ∮ E_ind · dl = −dΦ/dt. Electric field lines form closed loops!
Growth & Decay of Current in LR Circuit: Growth: I(t) = I₀ [1 − e^(−t / τ)]; Decay: I(t) = I₀ e^(−t / τ), where inductive time constant τ = L / R.
Dimensions Trap: L/R and CR have the dimension of TIME: [M⁰L⁰T¹]. √(LC) also has dimension of TIME.
Coil Turnover Trap: When a coil of N turns and area A in field B is rotated by 180°: Flux change ΔΦ = 2 NBA ⟹ Charge flown q = 2 NBA / R.
